title: Attention kernel lifecycle inspector and replay harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Recent canaries show intermittent latency and token-level regressions when switching kernels between FlashAttention v2 and v3 during high-concurrency prefill bursts. Root cause unclear: hypotheses include startup workspace fragmentation, KV cache warming mismatch, and kernel selection oscillation under multi-tenant noise. Goal: build an inspector that tracks kernel lifecycle events (selection, warmup, eviction, fallback) across requests and a deterministic replay harness to reproduce and bisect regressions seen in production traffic slices.
acceptance_criteria: Inspector emits structured events for kernel selection, warmup completion, eviction, fallback, and prefill/decode handoffs with request-level correlation IDs
Replay harness can take a 1-minute production trace (tokens, timestamps, kernel decisions) and deterministically reproduce sequence on test cluster
End-to-end test reproduces at least one real regression observed in canary with >95% fidelity compared to production telemetry
Documentation and runbook for using the harness to perform bisectes and developer-facing debug instructions are published in Confluence
tasks: Design event schema for kernel lifecycle inspector and add to runtime telemetry (Aisha)
Instrument runtime with lightweight ring-buffer per-worker to capture recent kernel events (Diego)
Add sampling and privacy filters to avoid PII in traces (Diego)
Build deterministic replay harness that can feed recorded requests and control kernel selection seed/state (Suresh)
Create synthetic testbed to inject prefill bursts and simulate multitenant noise patterns (Suresh)
Run bisect campaign on last 3 canary regressions and record root-cause hypotheses (team)
Write runbook and link example dashboards / query patterns (Aisha)
Create PRs and QA checklist; coordinate rollout of telemetry (Diego)
Postmortem template to capture findings and recommended runtime shims (team)

notes: Design trade-offs considered: attach full request bodies vs length-only hashes (chose hashes for privacy); synchronous vs asynchronous telemetry emission (chose async ring-buffer flush to avoid tail latency impact). We will start with conservative sampling and increase for targeted tenants during bisect runs.
next_steps: Complete deterministic seeding for allocator and kernel prober, run automated bisect across last five kernel commits, and prepare emergency rollback criteria if harness identifies unsafe kernel selector behaviors.
